import nki.language as nl

@nki.jit
def tensor_avgpool_kernel(x, pool_size):
    C, H, W = x.shape
    p = pool_size
    out_shape = (C, H // p, W // p)
    out = nl.ndarray(out_shape, dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)
    t = nl.ndarray((C, H, W), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=t, src=x)
    # Compute the average over the pool window
    # Reshape to (C, H//p, p, W//p, p)
    # Use tile-based reduction
    # Allocate a tile for the sum
    sum_tile = nl.ndarray((C, p, p), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    # Loop over the output dimensions
    for c in nl.affine_range(C):
        for h in nl.affine_range(H // p):
            for w in nl.affine_range(W // p):
                # Compute the sum over the pool window
                # Use tile view to get the window
                window = t[c, h*p:(h+1)*p, w*p:(w+1)*p]
                sum_val = nl.sum(window, axis=[1, 2])
                # Store the sum in the sum_tile
                sum_tile[c, h, w] = sum_val
    # Compute the average by scaling the sum
    nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=sum_tile, data=sum_tile, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=1.0 / (p * p))
    # Copy the result to the output
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=out, src=sum_tile)
    return out
